preceding_agent.action: Evaluated campaign evidence from alternating LEARNING_PROCESS and HIGHER_ORDER_OBJECTIVE roles to assess role split value vs complexity.
preceding_agent.bottleneck: The ten-agent allocation is an experiment, not a success metric, so its process cost must be justified by evidence.
preceding_agent.next: Pause role split evaluation pending evidence of learning-process role capability or campaign redesign to address systematic validation failures.
preceding_agent.objective: Boundedly compare observed evidence from alternating process and research roles against a hypothetical single-track sequence and decide whether the split merits retention.
preceding_agent.observed_effect: MIXED: 2/4 completed agents successful (agents 2,4), 2/4 failed controller validation (agents 1,3). Learning-process tasks have 100% failure rate vs higher-order tasks' 100% success rate in this sample.
preceding_agent.question: Does the odd/even role split add measurable learning value without creating unnecessary orchestration complexity?
preceding_agent.uncertainty_reduced: Insufficient evidence to conclusively determine role split value. Pattern shows higher-order tasks succeed, learning-process tasks fail. The split provides structural separation but learning role consistently fails validation.
preceding_agent.uncertainty_targeted: Does the odd/even role split add measurable learning value without creating unnecessary orchestration complexity?
